audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) A male narrator's voice begins with high clarity and a professional broadcast tone at a moderate conversational speed. The background music consists of classical orchestral strings playing a rhythmic, major-mode accompaniment at approximately 110 BPM, creating an educational atmosphere. (2) The narration remains stable as the speaker discusses music history. The BGM ducks in volume significantly to ensure vocal dominance while maintaining its steady rhythmic pulse in the low-frequency range of the mix. (3) Two sharp percussive hits representing cannon fire are heard, characterized by high spectral density and a sudden increase in amplitude. These SFX are precisely synchronized with the narrator's specific mention of powerful orchestral openings. (4) A short snippet of a female operatic vocal is heard singing the "Ode to Joy" melody. The voice exhibits classical vibrato and a bright, resonant timbre. The narrator's speech continues as a low-volume layer during this brief musical highlight. (5) The narrator's tone becomes more somber and reflective as he speaks about Beethoven's deafness. The BGM texture becomes warmer and less rhythmic, emphasizing melodic cello and string pads to match the emotional weight of the narrative. (6) A sharp audio transition leads to the outro, where a more energetic piano-driven musical piece swells in volume. The narration stops, allowing the promotional music to occupy the full dynamic range of the master track for the final three seconds.
